headline: KOSPI -4.88% to 6,273.66 as memory names give back Friday's historic rally: Samsung -8.19% (KRW 241,000), SK hynix -7.92% (KRW 1.582M); foreigners net-sold KRW 1.11T; brokerages trim PTs but 'no peak-out' — pure profit-take
summary: South Korea's KOSPI slid 4.88% to 6,273.66 on Monday, retracing part of Friday's record-setting 17.91% rally. Samsung Electronics closed -8.19% at KRW 241,000 and SK hynix fell 7.92% to KRW 1.582M. Foreign investors were net sellers of KRW 1.11T and institutions offloaded KRW 247B, while retail bought KRW 1.32T. Analysts framed the move as pure profit-taking after the previous session's blowoff, not thesis breakage — one strategist said the correction reflects 'excessive concentration' rather than 'peak-out concerns' on the HBM/AI-memory cycle. Several major desks cut near-term price targets on both names, though the medium-term memory supercycle read-through from AMZN/MSFT/AAPL memory-supply commentary last week remains intact. Softens the pre-market bid for MU / MPWR / SMH after Friday's rip.

headline: Brent -7.3% to $81.55 / WTI -5.9% to $79.66 after Trump calls off Iran strikes and announces Monday nuclear talks at Saudi/UAE/Qatar request; S&P futures +0.6%, EU +0.8% on cleaner risk backdrop into PLTR earnings
summary: Oil prices tumbled Monday after President Trump called off a 'massive' planned strike on Iran, saying Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar and Iran itself had asked him to pursue a deal — and announced fresh US-Iran nuclear talks would begin Monday. Brent for October fell as much as 7.3% to $81.55; WTI September lost nearly 6% to $79.66. S&P 500 futures rose ~0.6% and European futures ~0.8%. Iran's foreign ministry publicly cast doubt on direct negotiations, so the diplomatic window is fragile. The tape sets up a broad risk-on Monday open — supportive for growth/AI cohort into Palantir's after-close print and this week's AMD (Tue AMC), Siemens Energy (Wed), CEG (Thu), VST (Fri) reports. Datacenter power names (VST/CEG/GEV/VRT/ETN) may see profit-take on lower crude/energy-security bid; memory/hyperscaler complex helped by lower rates path.

headline: PLTR reports Q2 tonight AMC; Street models rev $1.81B (+81% YoY), EPS $0.34 (+113%); Oppenheimer sees ~85% growth; options price ~12-15% swing; Citi cuts PT to $200 from $225 (Buy); stock +2.75% pre-market, still ~30% off 2026 highs
summary: Palantir posts Q2 after Monday's close (5pm ET webcast). Consensus: revenue $1.81B (+81% YoY, US Commercial cited as the swing factor) and EPS $0.34 vs $0.16 YoY. Oppenheimer models ~85% growth, well above management's prior ~79% guide. Palantir has beaten EPS 8 quarters running, but Q1 fell 14% after the print, so setup is 'beat-and-hold' more than 'beat-and-rip.' Ahead of the print, Citigroup lowered its price target to $200 from $225 while maintaining Buy — the second straight quarter of PT trims on valuation. Consensus Overweight, PT ~$190. Options market pricing a 12-15% earnings move (~$16 straddle). Stock +2.75% pre-market on positive-tape / open-model letter tailwind, still ~30% below Feb 2026 highs. Read-through into AI-software cohort (SNOW/CRWD/AI/AAOI) if AIP / Warp Speed manufacturing wins re-accelerate US Commercial.

headline: Week ahead heavy tape: AMD Q2 Tue AMC ($11.2B guide, +47% YoY; Street EPS $1.61, +235%) — MI350/MI450 datacenter print in focus; SNDK Wed (first pure NAND read since -53% drawdown); CEG Thu; VST Fri; SIE.DE Q3 Wed
summary: Post-mega-cap earnings, this week hands the AI-infra baton to the datacenter chip/memory chain and to power names. AMD reports Tuesday Aug 4 AMC — guided Q2 rev $11.2B ±$300M (+47% YoY) with Street EPS $1.61 vs $0.48 YoY (+235%). Focus is MI350 (Helios) ramp cadence, MI450 tape-out signals, and any framing of the Broadcom-designed OpenAI inference silicon program impacting AMD's TAM narrative. SanDisk (SNDK) reports Wed — first pure-play NAND print since the stock fell 53% from ATH; tests whether Samsung/Micron memory-tightness commentary translates to actual NAND ASP inflection. Siemens Energy fiscal Q3 Wed pre-market (guide already raised to 14-16% growth / 10-12% margin). Constellation Energy (CEG) Thu pre with 10am ET call — three-signal watch: PJM capacity price stack, TMI restart schedule, and any new hyperscaler PPA. Vistra (VST) Fri pre — Street EPS $2.02 on rev $6.29B; near 52-wk lows into the print.

headline: AMZN raises 2026 cash capex to ~$220B (+$20B) with Jassy: 'we will still not have enough capacity in 2026… also true in 2027; 2028 demand is striking'; AWS RPO (backlog) $496B (+$132B QoQ, +30%); memory-cost inflation cited as key incremental driver
summary: Weekend digest of AMZN's Q2 print: Amazon lifted 2026 cash capex to roughly $220B (from ~$200B), attributing the incremental $20B primarily to higher DRAM/NAND memory input costs and continued AI infrastructure buildout. CEO Andy Jassy told analysts the company 'will still not have enough capacity to meet all the demand we have in 2026' and that the same will be 'true in 2027, too — in fact, the demand we already have for 2028 is striking.' CFO Brian Olsavsky added that 2027 AWS capacity is 'largely reserved' and 2028 slots are already being spoken for. AWS RPO backlog hit $496B, up $132B QoQ (+30%). Compounding factors — $220B capex + demand pull to 2028 + AAPL's memory-crunch guide — reinforce the multi-year TAM for NVDA / AVGO / MU / SK hynix / Samsung / MPWR / VRT / ETN / GEV / CEG / VST. Slight negative FCF signal but the AWS $169B ARR/38% margin easily supports it.

headline: Combined 2026 hyperscaler capex now tracking ~$740B (+77% YoY vs ~$410B in 2025): AMZN ~$220B, GOOG $195-205B, META $125-145B, MSFT ~$120B; 2027 datacenter capex tracking $1T+ per Motley Fool / Futurum
summary: Post-earnings, the Big Four hyperscaler 2026 capex composite has now been re-marked to roughly $740B — up ~77% from ~$410B in 2025 — after Amazon's $220B print and Google/Meta prior-week raises. Component levels: AMZN ~$220B, GOOG $195-205B, META $125-145B, MSFT ~$120B. Multiple sell-side notes (Motley Fool, Futurum, Forbes 'capex vigilantes') see 2027 crossing $1T. This is the cleanest confirmation yet that the AI-infra ROI dispute (which cracked the tape in late July on China DUV/NVDA circular-financing worries) has been decisively resolved in favor of the demand-real camp. Direct beneficiaries: NVDA (GPU volume), AVGO/MRVL (custom XPU), TSM (foundry), SK hynix/Samsung/MU (HBM/DRAM/NAND), MPWR (power ICs), VRT/ETN/GEV/SIE.DE (electrical & thermal), CEG/VST/TLN (behind-meter baseload), and increasingly ORCL (Stargate 4.5GW additive).

headline: TSMC's raised 2026 capex to $60-64B (+$8B) starts filtering through supply chain; JPM/Bloomberg consensus PT ~$490; July monthly revenue due ~Aug 10; TSM shares -~17% from Q2-print highs on capex/margin worry despite ~40% YTD
summary: Digest of TSMC's post-Q2 guide (July 16): full-year 2026 capex range lifted to $60-64B from prior $52-56B, plus the $265B U.S. build-out plan. Post-print, TSM traded off ~17% on aggressive-capex / margin-compression concern, though the consensus 12-mo target is ~$490 (Strong Buy) and JPMorgan flagged the pullback as a buying opportunity into the AI cycle. Next material catalyst is July monthly revenue release ~Aug 10 (June was NT$442.68B, +67.9% YoY). Read-across: ASML (EUV capacity monetization), AMAT/LRCX (WFE spend into gate-all-around, HBM DRAM tools), Vertiv/ETN (fab & datacenter electrical), and validates the memory-supercycle framing for SK hynix/Samsung/MU. The $265B U.S. plan is also a structural GEV / SIE.DE / ETN order pipeline for grid+substation.

headline: Nuclear-power PPA tracker at ~9.8 GW across 13 announced hyperscaler deals (May snapshot): META largest at ~6.6 GW (TerraPower/Oklo/VST); AMZN-TLN 1,920MW to 2042; MSFT-CEG 835MW TMI restart pulled to 2027; GOOG 1,800MW Elementl — Meta Louisiana 5GW facility scoping continues
summary: Weekend Carnegie/DCD tracker recap: hyperscaler nuclear PPA commitments have reached ~9.8 GW across 13 disclosed deals. Meta is the largest cumulative procurer at ~6.6 GW (2.2 GW Vistra Ohio/PA + TerraPower + Oklo option). Amazon-Talen: expanded to 1,920 MW through 2042 at Susquehanna (SMR expansion in scoping). Microsoft-Constellation: 20-year, $16B PPA to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1 (835 MW), first power now targeted for 2027 following the FERC waiver. Google: 1,800 MW Elementl Power deal. Meta's 5GW Louisiana facility scoping continues. Nine of the 13 projects rely on 2027-2031 first-power dates, so PJM/MISO gas-baseload PPA opportunity remains open near-term (positive VST, TLN). Also net-positive for CCJ / UEC uranium contract prices, and for BWXT (SMR pressure vessels) and NuScale (only NRC-approved SMR design as of Aug 2026).

headline: Semiconductor sector sales set another monthly record: SIA global sales $120.6B in May +104.1% YoY (15th consecutive record); Broadcom guiding AI semi rev >200% YoY to $16B this quarter; Micron $50B quarterly rev run-rate track
summary: Semiconductor Industry Association reported global semi sales of $120.6B in May, +104.1% YoY, the 15th consecutive monthly record. Broadcom's most recent guide implies AI semiconductor revenue growth of >200% YoY to $16.0B this quarter; Micron is on a track toward a $50B quarterly revenue run-rate. The absolute-record + still-accelerating YoY comps are the structural counterpoint to Monday's KOSPI profit-take and to the July 29 chip-selloff narrative — the tape volatility is largely positioning, not fundamental deterioration. Setup positive for AMD Tuesday AMC print and NVDA later this month. Watch: hyperscaler capex commentary, Micron shipment tracking, and Credo (CRDO) execution as the three key August catalysts per the sell-side. Read-across also to AMAT, LRCX, KLAC (WFE), and MPWR / MRVL / AVGO for AI power/silicon exposure.

headline: Amazon files with Virginia SCC to let hyperscalers voluntarily fund transmission for large datacenter campuses — direct-pay framework would blunt residential rate backlash that's stalled buildout permitting in NoVa/Loudoun; positive read for GEV / ETN / QNT / SIE.DE utility-scale grid tenders
summary: Amazon has asked Virginia utility regulators to formally allow hyperscalers to voluntarily fund the transmission and substation upgrades required to serve their datacenter campuses, rather than socializing those costs onto retail ratepayers. The proposal is a direct response to the political backlash in NoVa/Loudoun County over hyperscaler-driven power-cost inflation on residential customers. If approved by the SCC, the model likely becomes a template for other PJM/MISO/ERCOT jurisdictions and materially accelerates permit timelines for the ~30 GW datacenter pipeline. Positive read for the grid-equipment cohort: GEV (HVDC + transformers), ETN (switchgear/data-hall electrical, +18% Q2 EMEA organic), SIE.DE (grid backlog €146B), QNT/Hubbell/Prysmian (transmission conductor/cable), and for VST/CEG/TLN behind-meter offtake economics. Slightly negative for utility-side rate-base compounders (NEE, D, DUK) that could otherwise put the transmission spend into base.
